survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD PISA 2022 factsheet reports descriptive and benchmark results derived from the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The underlying PISA design is a complex, stratified sampling of schools and students within participating countries/economies, and OECD typically provides sampling weights and replicate weights for variance estimation in the database. The factsheet itself does not specify which weight variable (e.g., student sampling weight) or which replicate method (e.g., BRR/jackknife) was applied in the computations shown. Analysts using the OECD PISA 2022 Database should apply the provided complex-survey weights and replicate weights when reproducing standard errors and confidence intervals for mean scores and proficiency-level shares.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This factsheet is a descriptive reporting of PISA 2022 results (means, trends, and proficiency-level percentages) rather than an empirical study that models outcomes with a specified PV-based dependent variable. Plausible values are used within PISA scaling and the OECD database to produce achievement estimates, but the factsheet does not document a specific PV combining rule for any re-estimation step by the authors. Missing-data handling is therefore not reported at the factsheet level because the computations rely on OECD’s established PISA data processing pipeline rather than a bespoke analysis described in the document.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic sample reported for Malta includes 15-year-old students who completed the PISA 2022 assessment in mathematics, reading, or science: 3,127 students in 46 schools. The factsheet does not describe additional exclusions beyond the standard PISA participation and quality standards; it states that all Malta data met PISA quality standards and were fit for reporting.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 factsheet summarizes how Malta’s 15-year-old students performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results changed over time (notably 2018–2022 and longer trends since 2012). Students took two two-hour tests with different item sets across students, and they also completed a background questionnaire; the factsheet reports mean performance and proficiency-level shares (e.g., Level 2 and Level 5/6) using OECD’s PISA 2022 Database tables. For Malta, average results were about the same as in 2018 in mathematics and reading, and higher in science; over 2012–2022, results did not show a clear improvement or deterioration in all three subjects. Malta scored below the OECD average in all three domains, with smaller proportions of top performers and fewer students reaching minimum proficiency across all three subjects. The document also highlights within-country gaps by socio-economic status and gender, and reports contextual indicators such as belonging, discipline in mathematics lessons, safety, parental involvement, and COVID-related learning experiences.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is an OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet that reports descriptive statistics and benchmark comparisons rather than an empirical machine-learning or predictive modeling study. As a result, there is no target variable modeled with ML, no PV-handling or missing-data strategy specified for re-analysis, and no model performance metrics (e.g., accuracy/AUC/RMSE) to extract. The extraction therefore leaves main_findings and confounders_identified empty because the factsheet does not present an analytical pipeline with predictors and outcomes.
